subject: Post-call: projected burn scenarios, $/1M target & startup program application
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@waypointai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + a couple quick asks on volume and $/1M target

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking time today — really appreciate the candid rundown on where Waypoint is headed with agent-driven search and the embed-heavy vector store workflows. Quick recap and two asks so we can scope a crisp committed-use proposal: 

Recap:
- Primary workloads: contextual search + reranking for product docs, chat assist for CS, nightly batch embeddings for new content.
- Current pilot: 0.8–1.2M tokens/day (mostly generation + embeddings) with a spike profile during business hours.
- Desired SLO: p95 generation < 300ms for interactive flows.

Two asks to firm up pricing options:
1) Ballpark monthly token ranges you expect over the next 3–12 months (e.g., 1–5M/mo / 5–20M/mo / 20–50M/mo). This lets me propose starter bands vs committed tiers.
2) Target unit economics — what is your target $/1M tokens (or your budget range) for a committed path vs. a self-serve rate? If you have a hard target (e.g., $1,500–$2,000 per 1M tokens) call it out.

I attached a short burn-scenarios.xlsx with three ramp profiles (pilot, scale, aggressive) and a placeholder three-year term sheet to show how multi-year incentives could look. Separately, if you plan to apply for our startup program, attach the one-pager and I’ll route the application (startup seats usually include an extra 15–25% credit in year one).

Proposed next step: If you can reply with the two datapoints above this week, I’ll share a pricing sketch (starter + committed 6/12/36mo tier) and a recommended discount path for startup + multi-year incentives. Happy to jump on a 20m call with procurement if that helps.

Thanks —
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: burn-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Elena Park <elena@waypointai.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + a couple quick asks on volume and $/1M target

Thanks Mateo — great write-up and exactly the structure I wanted. Quick answers below — forwarding to procurement on the cc.

Ballpark token ranges (next 12 months):
- Months 0–3 (pilot): ~30–40M tokens total (about 1–1.5M/day)
- Months 4–9 (ramping): ~120–150M total (4–6M/day average, spikes to 10M/day)
- Months 10–12+: targeting 300–400M total (10–15M/day steady state)

Budget / target $/1M:
- We’re aiming for ~$1,600–$2,200 per 1M tokens on committed pricing to make the unit economics work for our pricing model.
- If the committed discount gets us to <$1,600 that would be ideal.

Program ask: Yes, we intend to apply for the startup program. I’m including procurement here (procurement@waypointai.com) so you can send any required intake form.

Timeline: Procurement aims to review vendor pricing options next week and surface recommendations by 10/18.

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Product | Waypoint AI
elena@waypointai.com

Thanks Elena — that ramp is helpful and clearer than the high-level signals in the call. A couple of notes and next steps from our side: 

1) Startup program: Please complete the attached startup-application.pdf and we’ll fast-track through our partner ops team. Startup path typically adds a one-time credit and priority onboarding — I’ll estimate the effective % headroom against committed tiers.

2) Committed pricing options: I attached a 3yr-term-sheet.pdf that outlines a 12/24/36mo committed model at a few example unit rates. With the ramp you described, my initial thinking:
   - Pilot (months 0–3): recommend a month-to-month or small 3mo partial commitment to avoid blocking runway.
   - Ramp (months 4–9): a 12mo committed tier with step-down pricing once you hit higher bands.
   - Steady (post-12mo): 24–36mo commitment to secure deeper unit discounts and multi-year incentives (we can layer a rebate schedule tied to volume milestones).

3) Pricing ask: You noted $1,600–$2,200 target. I’ve CC’d Ben (pricing lead) and Marissa (program ops) to align on an illustrative discount path that reaches toward the $1,600/1M neighborhood with a startup credit + 36mo structure. Ben — can you confirm the maximum starter discount we can pair with the program (thinking 15–25% starter + 10% multi-year target) and whether we should surface an escrowed rebate for the 3yr path?

If procurement is comfortable, can we get a 30–45 minute pricing review next Tue (10/12) to run a numbers walk? I’ll bring the costing scenarios.

Regards,
Mateo

Attachments: startup-application.pdf, 3yr-term-sheet.pdf
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Waypoint pricing posture — quick approval request

Marissa / Ben —

Summary of external ask: Waypoint expects to ramp from ~30–40M (pilot) to 300–400M/year by month 12. They signaled a target ~$1,600–$2,200 per 1M on committed pricing and want to apply to the startup program. Procurement timeline: review complete by 10/18.

Proposed commercial posture (for approval):
- Year 1: offer an initial committed discount band that gets median unit to ~$1,800/1M for the 12mo ramp window (this assumes a startup credit equivalent to ~18% off list).
- Multi-year incentive: contingent 10% rebate spread over years 2–3 if cumulative annual volume >= 700M tokens.
- Early-stage protection: 60-day exit window for the first 3 months if usage remains < 30M total (reduces risk for them).

Ask: Ben — can you sign off on the 18% starter credit + 10% multi-year rebate construct as a pre-approved sketch to share with procurement? If not, what caps do we need to observe? Marissa — if you confirm startup program eligibility once they return the application, I’ll route partner credits into the sketch.

Thanks — Mateo
